chapter: Meeting Louis and the New Orleans bands
title: Staying at Jack Carey's coal place
summary: Punch lodged free in a coal shed owned by Jack Carey, whose band he joined; he slept on the daybed.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Where were you staying then? In a boarding house?

No, I was living in a place called Jack Kerry. He had a wooden coal place, and I was playing, I joined his bands, and he gave me a place to stay there. But it was pretty sad, though. Yeah. Oh, no, it was sad. It was sad.
How much did Jack call you, charge you to stay there?
He didn't charge me nothing. I was playing the band with him, and he just gave me the place to sleep.
And you slept on the coal side? Yeah. No, did you? What did you sleep on? The day count.
The day count, yeah. He shut it up in the day and opened it up at night, you know. Oh, yeah.
